key_insight: A simple logarithmic radiance encoding plus lightweight latent alignment lets existing generative models produce faithful HDR video without re-training large HDR-specific representations — leveraging pre-trained visual priors instead of learning HDR from scratch.
problem_solved: Generative models are typically trained on bounded, perceptually compressed (LDR) data and fail to reproduce true scene radiance; this work addresses the mismatch between HDR radiance and those model priors, enabling HDR video synthesis with far less data and complexity.
method: Apply a logarithmic encoding to HDR radiance so its dynamic range matches the statistics the pretrained generator expects.
Learn a compact latent alignment/mapping between encoded HDR frames and the generator's latent space (adapter network or alignment objective) rather than re-training full HDR representations.
Enforce temporal consistency in the latent domain for coherent HDR video output (temporal losses or latent smoothing) and decode back to HDR for evaluation and tone-mapped visualization.
impact: Practitioners can generate high-fidelity HDR video using off-the-shelf generative models with minimal extra data and compute, simplifying HDR content creation and enabling better radiometric realism in downstream applications like VFX, virtual production, and image-based lighting.

paper_title: HDR Video Generation via Latent Alignment with Logarithmic Encoding
paper_authors: Naomi Ken Korem, Mohamed Oumoumad, Harel Cain, Matan Ben Yosef, Urska Jelercic
